bio_md:
# 汉元帝 · 主要事迹

刘奭是[[han-xuan-di|汉宣帝]]之子，立为太子时宣帝已有隐忧：太子柔仁好儒，宣帝曾叹「乱我家者太子也」。黄龙元年宣帝崩，奭即位，西汉由此从「霸王道杂之」的实干政治转向儒生政治——而这正是西汉由盛转衰的节点。

元帝朝开初尚有一番气象：征用贡禹等儒生，议罢甘泉、建章宫卫，减省用度；但政令渐成具文，优游不断成了元帝的痼疾。中书令石显乘机弄权，朝政壅蔽。武功方面，永光二年冯奉世击陇西羌，建昭三年甘延寿、陈汤矫制发兵，斩郅支单于于康居——「明犯强汉者，虽远必诛」的豪语即出于此役，然皆臣下之力，帝无所与。

竟宁元年，呼韩邪单于入朝请婚，元帝以后宫良家子王昭君赐之，昭君出塞成为汉匈和亲的最后华章。同年五月，元帝崩，[[han-cheng-di|成帝]]即位。史称元帝「牵制文义，优游不断」，元成之世，外戚与宦官问题相继累积，汉室之衰自此而始。

> 参考：点校本《汉书》卷009《元帝纪》、卷094《匈奴传》，《贡禹传》、《陈汤传》，谭图第 2 册。

bio_parts_en.value: Liu Shi was the son of

. Even when Shi was made heir apparent, Xuan had misgivings: the heir was gentle and devoted to Confucian learning, and Xuan once sighed that "the one who will throw my house into disorder is the heir apparent." When Xuan died in the first Huanglong year, Shi succeeded, and Western Han turned from the pragmatic "mixed way of king and hegemon" to Confucian politics — the hinge of the dynasty's decline.

His reign opened with some promise: Confucian scholars such as Gong Yu were summoned, and the garrisons of the Ganquan and Jianzhang palaces were debated and trimmed. But the edicts dissolved into formalism, and irresolution became Yuan's chronic ailment; Shi Xian, chief of the Inner Secretariat, seized power and clogged the court. On the frontier, Feng Fengshi crushed a Qiang revolt in Longxi in the second Yongguang year, and in the third Jianzhao year Gan Yanshou and Chen Tang, acting on their own authority, slew the Zhizhi chanyu in Kangju — the boast "whoever offends mighty Han shall be punished, however distant" dates from that campaign — yet all was the work of ministers, with the emperor having no part.

In the first Jingning year the Huhanye chanyu came to court seeking a bride, and Yuan granted him the palace woman Wang Zhaojun; her departure became the last great chapter of Han-Xiongnu marriage alliance. In the fifth month of the same year, Yuan died and

succeeded. The historians wrote that Yuan was "fettered by the letter of the classics, irresolute to the end"; in the Yuan-Cheng age, consort-clan and eunuch problems accumulated in turn, and the decline of the house of Han began here.

> References: the punctuated critical edition of the *Hanshu*, ch. 9 (Benji of Emperor Yuan), ch. 94 (Treatise on the Xiongnu), and the biographies of Gong Yu and Chen Tang; Tan Qixiang's atlas, vol. 2.
